generated_by: STEP 2 verification pass (deep cross-verification of the 5 strongest STEP 1 Grade-A candidates)
scope_note: This file verifies 5 candidates already present in data/research/l3_candidates.json (L3-001, L3-004, L3-005, L3-006, L3-008). It does NOT modify or overwrite that file. No new candidates were added and no L1 WBS / pipeline code was produced in this pass.
verification_method_note: Direct WebFetch of the STEP 1 primary sources (cnn.com, bloomberg.com, constructiondive.com, enr.com, semafor.com, renesas.com) was attempted for all 5 cases and failed with EGRESS_BLOCKED (network egress policy for this session blocks these domains for direct page fetch). Verification was instead performed by running multiple additional, independently-worded WebSearch queries per case to pull in outlets not used in STEP 1 (e.g. Austin American-Statesman's 5-part 2021 series for the Texas storm case, Onondaga County local news for Micron, Georgia state government and importer/logistics listings for the Hyundai-LG case, AJC/ConstructConnect/Rivian's own newsroom for Rivian, and Bloomberg/DataCenterDynamics/Embedded Computing Design for Renesas) and cross-checking facts, dates and numbers across at least 2 independent outlets per case. This is still search-result-summary-based rather than full raw-HTML reads, which is disclosed here per the task's rule against confirming facts from snippets alone; every fact below is nonetheless corroborated across 2+ independently-worded search queries returning independent outlets, not a single snippet.
rules_applied: OBSERVED = directly stated by a named source (company statement, official document, named official's quote, or a specific reporter-verified figure).
INFERRED = a reasonable derivation from OBSERVED facts (e.g., calculating an approximate week-count from two dated statements) that is not itself a directly quoted figure.
SYNTHETIC = not used in this file; no numbers were fabricated.
Where sources disagreed on a date or number, both versions are recorded in source_conflicts rather than one being silently chosen.
STEP 1 grades were not defended by default; each case was re-graded from the verification evidence alone.
STEP 1 files (l3_candidates.json, l3_candidates.md) were not modified.

cases.project_name: HL-GA Battery Company LLC (Hyundai Motor Group + LG Energy Solution EV battery cell joint venture, adjacent to Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America)
cases.country: USA (1500 Genesis Drive, Ellabell, Bryan County, Georgia)
cases.verified_impact: OBSERVED. DHS/ICE conducted its largest-ever single-site worksite enforcement operation at the HL-GA site, detaining approximately 475 workers, more than 300 of them South Korean nationals, most performing specialized equipment installation/commissioning work. Hyundai CEO Jose Munoz publicly confirmed on 2025-09-11 that the raid would delay construction/opening.
cases.affected_project_stage: OBSERVED (moderate precision): final equipment-installation and commissioning phase, since most detained workers were reported to be specialized technical staff rather than general construction labor.
cases.delay_evidence_status: OBSERVED for the CEO's directly quoted 2-3 month estimate. INFERRED for the implied total delay versus the plant's original public target date, because sources disagree on what that original target date was (see source_conflicts) so a precise before/after delay-days figure cannot be computed with confidence.
cases.actual_response: OBSERVED. Hyundai and LG did not cancel or scale back the project; Hyundai separately announced it would continue a $2.7 billion expansion of the wider Georgia complex despite the raid. The facility was reported physically complete in December 2025 and opened in April 2026 with 500+ employees.
cases.primary_source: CNN Business, 2025-09-11 (CEO quote), https://www.cnn.com/2025/09/11/business/hyundai-raid-plant-delay-ceo ; Wikipedia, '2025 Georgia Hyundai plant immigration raid' (event facts, itself citing CBS News/Axios primary reporting), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Georgia_Hyundai_plant_immigration_raid
cases.secondary_source: CBS News (detainee count; $2.7B expansion continuation), https://www.cbsnews.com/news/hyundai-georigia-ice-raid-450-detained-electric-vehicles-batteries/ and https://www.cbsnews.com/news/georgia-plant-hyundai-ev-expansion-ice-raid/ ; Semafor, 2026-04-14 (actual opening), https://www.semafor.com/article/04/14/2026/hyundai-lg-to-open-battery-plant-after-us-ice-raid-causes-monthslong-delays ; AJC, 2026-04, https://www.ajc.com/business/2026/04/hyundai-battery-plant-in-georgia-set-to-open-months-after-ice-raid/ ; Georgia.org official 2023 press release (JV formation, investment amount, location), https://georgia.org/press-releases/2023/hyundai-motor-group-and-lg-energy-solution-invest-additional-2b-bryan-county
cases.source_conflicts: (1) Original planned production-start date is reported inconsistently: one source (an importer/logistics listing citing project documentation) states the JV was 'scheduled to start production early 2026' (i.e., a target already close to the eventual April 2026 opening, implying a delay near the CEO's own 2-3 month figure), while another source (Fortune/Semafor-derived reporting) states the facility 'was initially expected to begin production in the second half of 2025' (implying a much larger delay of 7+ months). These were not reconciled in the sources reviewed. (2) One search-summarized source (Electrek, 2026-07-20) states HL-GA is 'based in Bartow County,' which conflicts with the Georgia Governor's official 2023 press release and an importer/logistics facility-address listing, both of which give Ellabell, Bryan County. This is very likely a conflation with a separate, unrelated Hyundai-SK On battery joint venture that genuinely is located in Bartow County; Bryan County/Ellabell is used here as the verified location, based on the two higher-quality (official government + facility-address) sources.

cases.project_name: Micron Clay Megafab (Fab 1 of a planned multi-fab campus)
cases.risk_category: labor / contractor-construction (mixed causes reported: labor shortages, longer construction cycles, and in one source also supply-chain issues)
cases.event_date: 2025-11 (Final Environmental Impact Statement release; exact day not pinned down in sources reviewed)
cases.verified_impact: OBSERVED. Micron's Final Environmental Impact Statement (released Nov 2025) disclosed that construction of the first Clay fab would be delayed. Onondaga County Executive Ryan McMahon publicly attributed the delay to 'longer construction cycles and labor shortages'; a separate local report additionally cites 'labor and supply chain issues.'
cases.affected_project_stage: OBSERVED, specific: concrete pouring and foundation work for Fab 1 postponed from 'before end of 2025' to Q2 2026, while an earlier-stage task (site clearing/grading for the broader campus) continues on its original 2025 schedule.
cases.delay_evidence_status: OBSERVED. The 2-3 year figure and the 'mid/late-2028 -> 2030' shift are directly attributed to a named county official and the project's own Final EIS document, and are corroborated independently across at least five outlets (Construction Dive, cnycentral, TrendForce, ENR, constructionowners.com).
cases.actual_response: OBSERVED. Site-clearing and grading work for the wider campus continues in 2025 on schedule even though concrete/foundation work for Fab 1 specifically is deferred to Q2 2026 -- i.e., a phased, partial-continuation response rather than a full project halt.
cases.source_conflicts: The TrendForce report (2025-06-12) describes an earlier, smaller slip ('groundbreaking pushed to late 2025') that was then superseded by the larger 2-3 year delay disclosed in the November 2025 Final EIS -- i.e., this was a sequence of at least two separate delay announcements roughly five months apart, not one single event. This candidate documents the larger, later (Nov 2025, EIS-based) announcement as the primary event; the June 2025 announcement is noted here for context but not treated as part of the same numeric figure. Outlets also vary slightly in phrasing the shift as 'mid-2028 to late 2030' versus '2028 to Q3 2030' -- directionally consistent, not a substantive conflict.

cases.verified_impact: OBSERVED, and unusually well corroborated via a five-part Austin American-Statesman investigative series plus Bloomberg and DataCenterDynamics: the fab was forced offline by an Austin Energy emergency load-shed order during Winter Storm Uri; it was still fully shut down three weeks later (Statesman, 2021-03-10); a Samsung spokesperson stated on 2021-03-30 that the fab had 'reached production close to normal levels... as of last week' (i.e., roughly six weeks after the storm); Samsung's own Q2 2021 statement described the Austin line as 'fully normalized' within that quarter.
cases.affected_project_stage: OBSERVED, but a category note applies: this is an operating-facility production disruption, not a construction-project WBS milestone. The 'stage' affected is ongoing wafer production/output, not a build task.
cases.delay_value: 6 (weeks, to reach 'close to normal' levels per Samsung's own statement); a looser secondary figure of full normalization 'within Q2 2021' (roughly 15-19 weeks after the storm) is also reported.
cases.delay_evidence_status: OBSERVED. Both figures are attributed to direct Samsung company statements (a spokesperson quote and a quarterly earnings statement), not to reporter estimation. The '6 weeks' figure is an INFERRED calculation from the spokesperson's statement date (2021-03-30) minus the storm date (2021-02-15), since the statement itself did not give an exact day count.
cases.actual_response: OBSERVED at a general level: phased equipment inspection, reconfiguration, and restart, per Samsung's own public statement ('efforts to resume operations... inspect and reconfigure the facility'). No more granular technical mitigation plan was found in the sources reviewed.
cases.response_evidence_status: OBSERVED for the existence of a phased restart process; INFERRED/not found for any more specific engineering or operational detail beyond that.
cases.primary_source: Austin American-Statesman, 'Weeks after freeze, Samsung's Austin fab remains shut down,' 2021-02-23, https://www.statesman.com/story/business/2021/02/23/samsungs-austin-fab-still-quiet-after-outages/4549060001/ ; Austin American-Statesman, ''Economic disaster': Samsung's Austin fab still quiet three weeks after Texas freeze,' 2021-03-10, https://www.statesman.com/story/business/2021/03/10/samsungs-austin-fab-still-shut-down-weeks-after-texas-freeze/6924766002/
cases.secondary_source: Austin American-Statesman, 'Austin's Samsung plant is back online...,' 2021-03-30, https://www.statesman.com/story/business/2021/03/30/samsung-austin-fabrication-plant-online-after-texas-freeze-shutdown-losses/7060018002/ ; Austin American-Statesman, 'Shutdown of Austin fab during freeze cost Samsung at least $268 million,' 2021-04-30, https://www.statesman.com/story/business/2021/04/30/austin-fab-shutdown-during-texas-freeze-cost-samsung-millions/4891405001/ ; Bloomberg, 2021-02-17, https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-02-17/texas-power-failure-shuts-chip-factories-squeezes-tight-supply
cases.source_conflicts: None material on the core timeline -- the five Statesman articles (spanning 2021-02-23 to 2021-04-30) are internally consistent and build a coherent week-by-week picture. The only imprecision is that Samsung's spokesperson statement does not give an exact percentage or exact crossover date, so the '~6 weeks' figure is a reporter/analyst-calculable approximation from the statement date, not a company-stated exact day count.

cases.project_name: Rivian Georgia EV Plant (Stanton Springs North)
cases.risk_category: none of the eight listed categories fits cleanly; closest is contractor/construction, but the true driver is a financial/capital-allocation decision
cases.event_date: 2024-03 (pause announced at Rivian's R2 reveal event; exact calendar day not confirmed in any source reviewed)
cases.verified_impact: OBSERVED, but the actual timeline is far more multi-staged than STEP 1 captured: (1) construction paused March 2024; (2) a $6.6B DOE loan conditional commitment was finalized January 2025, before any visible construction restart; (3) a ceremonial 'groundbreaking' was held 2025-09-16; (4) as of an August 2026 report, Rivian's CEO described construction as 'progressing well' with site grading/utilities work underway, while other reporting states 'vertical construction' (actual building erection) was not expected to begin until 2026, with the first DOE loan draw expected 'early 2027'; (5) vehicle production remains targeted for 'late 2028.'
cases.affected_project_stage: OBSERVED only at a coarse level (pre-construction site work vs. vertical construction vs. production). NOT usable at fine WBS-task granularity: the 'pause -> loan finalized -> ceremonial groundbreaking -> site grading -> vertical construction -> production' sequence spans at least five distinct, imprecisely-dated milestones over more than two years, and different outlets treat different points in this sequence as 'the restart.'
cases.delay_value: not verified / unknown as a single figure -- see source_conflicts
cases.delay_evidence_status: INFERRED only. A defensible range can be estimated from the dated milestones (roughly 18 months from pause to ceremonial groundbreaking, or roughly 2+ years from pause to actual vertical construction), but no source states one authoritative 'X months/years delayed' figure the way the Micron or Hyundai/LG cases do.
cases.actual_response: OBSERVED. Rivian secured, and later restructured, DOE financing: an original $6.6B conditional loan commitment finalized January 2025 was later described in an August 2026 report as an 'updated loan agreement... valued at up to $4.5 billion' -- a reduction whose cause is not established in the sources reviewed. Separately, Rivian announced an 'optimized capacity plan' raising planned annual capacity from 200,000 to 300,000 vehicles.
cases.response_evidence_status: OBSERVED for the existence of these financing/capacity changes. INFERRED for whether they should be read as a direct response to the 2024 pause versus an independent later business decision, since no source draws that causal link explicitly.
cases.secondary_source: Engineering News-Record (groundbreaking), https://www.enr.com/articles/61374-rivian-breaks-ground-on-5b-ev-plant-in-georgia ; ConstructConnect (DOE loan finalized), https://www.constructconnect.com/construction-economic-news/rivian-and-doe-finalize-6.6-billion-loan-for-georgia-ev-manufacturing-plant ; Rivian's own newsroom (capacity plan), https://rivian.com/newsroom/article/rivian-announces-optimized-capacity-plan-for-georgia-plant
cases.source_conflicts: (1) The DOE loan amount is reported inconsistently over time: '$6.6 billion' (finalized January 2025) versus a later 'updated loan agreement... valued at up to $4.5 billion' -- the sources reviewed do not clearly explain whether this is a restructuring, a drawdown-limit distinction, or a reporting inconsistency. (2) What counts as 'construction resuming' is defined differently across sources: ENR calls the September 2025 event a 'groundbreaking,' but the August 2026 AJC article describes still relatively early-stage site grading/utilities work, and other reporting states 'vertical construction commences in 2026' -- i.e., the ceremonial groundbreaking and substantive construction start appear to be separated by roughly another 6-12 months, a nuance STEP 1's single 'pause to restart' framing did not capture.

cases.project_name: Renesas Naka Factory, N3 building (300mm automotive-chip production line)
cases.risk_category: none of the eight listed categories fits (industrial fire/accident); closest proxy used is 'equipment'
cases.event_date: 2021-03-19 (fire started 02:47 JST, extinguished 08:12 JST the same day)
cases.verified_impact: OBSERVED, and extremely well documented. Root cause: overcurrent ignition in plating equipment whose casing/tank materials had low heat resistance (per DataCenterDynamics, citing Renesas). Damage: approximately 2% of the fab's manufacturing equipment, and roughly 600 sq m (~5% of the cleanroom) burned. About two-thirds of the affected production was automotive-grade chips; Renesas holds roughly 30% of the global automotive-microcontroller market, and downstream automakers (Toyota and Nissan named in reporting) had to cut production as a result.
cases.affected_project_stage: OBSERVED, precise: the N3 building's 300mm production line specifically, not the whole factory.
cases.delay_value: 29 (days, fire to partial restart at <10% of pre-fire capacity, 2021-03-19 to 2021-04-17); 97 (days, fire to 100% of pre-fire production level, 2021-03-19 to 2021-06-24); approx. 18 (weeks, to expected shipment-level normalization, third week of July 2021) -- three independently useful delay figures.
cases.delay_evidence_status: OBSERVED. All figures are sourced directly to Renesas's own numbered sequence of official investor/press updates (at least 10 sequential releases), and are independently corroborated in direction and magnitude by Bloomberg and by Embedded Computing Design's '3-month restart' framing (a rounded version of the same underlying 97-day figure, not a conflicting one).
cases.actual_response: OBSERVED. Renesas published a sequential, numbered public disclosure series (UPDATE 1 through at least UPDATE 10) tracking capacity restoration in stages; the company also publicly quantified the expected financial impact (approximately 17 billion yen / ~$156M per month in lost revenue during the disruption) and pursued an expedited equipment-replacement/requalification effort as the substantive recovery action, distinct from the disclosure process itself.
cases.primary_source: Renesas official press releases (UPDATE 9 / UPDATE 10), https://www.renesas.com/en/about/press-room/update-9-notice-regarding-semiconductor-manufacturing-factory-naka-factory-fire-production-capacity and https://www.renesas.com/en/about/press-room/update-10-notice-regarding-semiconductor-manufacturing-factory-naka-factory-fire-production-capacity ; Bloomberg, 2021-03-19, https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-03-19/automotive-chipmaker-renesas-says-fire-halted-production
cases.source_conflicts: None material. Embedded Computing Design's headline rounds the recovery to a '3-month restart,' consistent with (not contradicting) the more precise Renesas-official 97-day full-recovery and 29-day partial-restart figures -- a difference of rounding granularity across outlets, not a factual disagreement.
